bug_description.normalized: The staged HEIF witness reaches `vips_foreign_load_heif_set_header()`, where libvips asks libheif for a metadata block's size and type. On the reproduced crash path, the block is typed `exif` and the saved ASan allocation context shows the reported metadata size was only 1 byte. Vulnerable `heifload.c` still executes `data += 4; length -= 4` to skip the EXIF offset prefix without checking `length >= 4`, moving the metadata pointer four bytes past the 1-byte allocation and wrapping the unsigned `length` to a huge value. That invalid pointer/length pair is stored as `VIPS_META_EXIF_NAME`, automatically reparsed by `vips__exif_parse()`, and forwarded into libexif. `exif_data_load_data()` therefore bypasses its `ds < 6` short-buffer return and calls `memcmp(d, ExifHeader, 6)` on the out-of-bounds pointer, which AddressSanitizer reports as a 6-byte heap-buffer-overflow read.

source.code:
size_t length = heif_image_handle_get_metadata_size( heif->handle, id[i] );
const char *type = heif_image_handle_get_metadata_type( heif->handle, id[i] );
source.description: First non-harness project statement on the crashing path that materializes vulnerability-relevant state from the attacker-controlled HEIF metadata block: its reported byte length and metadata type.
source.value_from: The saved allocation context at `libvips/libvips/foreign/heifload.c:440` proves that the metadata block reaching this path had `length == 1`. The later EXIF-specific branch and automatic `vips__exif_parse()` call show that the same block's `type` compares equal to `"exif"`.

tainted_value_origin.code:
size_t length = heif_image_handle_get_metadata_size( heif->handle, id[i] );
const char *type = heif_image_handle_get_metadata_type( heif->handle, id[i] );
tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant state originates when libvips asks libheif for the current metadata block's size and type. On the witnessed block, libheif reports a 1-byte metadata payload and `type == "exif"`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: ASan's allocation stack ties the later 1-byte region directly to this `length` value, and the reproduced EXIF parse path proves the same metadata block is treated as EXIF.

root_cause.description: Within the EXIF-specific trim block, libvips subtracts 4 from unsigned `length` without first checking that the reported metadata block is at least 4 bytes long.
root_cause.note: With the witnessed `length == 1`, this wraps `length` to a huge `size_t` instead of rejecting the short EXIF block. The same unchecked block also executes `data += 4`, so the wrapped size is later paired with an already out-of-bounds pointer.

sink.description: ASan crash site. Libexif performs a 6-byte EXIF header comparison on the invalid pointer propagated from `heifload.c`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 6` at `libexif/libexif/exif-data.c:862:7`, address `0x602000016a34`, which is 3 bytes to the right of the 1-byte region `[0x602000016a30,0x602000016a31)` allocated at `libvips/libvips/foreign/heifload.c:440`.

parser_admitted.description: The crashing witness reaches a metadata block whose `type` string is treated as `"exif"`, so libvips enters the EXIF-specific metadata path. That same path later stores the blob under `VIPS_META_EXIF_NAME`, which `vips_image_set()` automatically reparses with `vips__exif_parse()`.

evidence_limitations: The staged `patch.diff` is unrelated documentation text rather than the reproduced crash fix, so Stage 02 did not use it to justify root cause or `patch_resolves`.

Stage 01 preserves the crashing stack and the 1-byte allocation context but not the raw one-byte EXIF metadata payload itself; the trace is therefore grounded on the observed length/type-driven state transitions rather than on specific metadata bytes.

coarse_trace.summary: libvips reads a HEIF metadata block's reported size and type from libheif, allocates a 1-byte buffer for that block, and copies the metadata bytes into it.

The EXIF-specific path strips a 4-byte prefix without checking `length >= 4`, producing an out-of-bounds pointer plus wrapped length, stores them as the image's EXIF blob, and automatically dispatches `vips__exif_parse()` for that blob.
EXIF parsing reloads the same blob pointer and wrapped `size_t`, narrows that size through `size_t -> int -> unsigned int`, and forwards the corrupted pointer/length pair into libexif.
Because libexif sees a huge wrapped `ds`, its `ds < 6` short-buffer guard does not fire, and `memcmp(d, ExifHeader, 6)` reads 6 bytes from the out-of-bounds pointer, matching the ASan crash.

fine_trace.code:
size_t length = heif_image_handle_get_metadata_size( heif->handle, id[i] );
const char *type = heif_image_handle_get_metadata_type( heif->handle, id[i] );
fine_trace.note: Source. For the metadata block that reaches the crashing path, libvips materializes `length` and `type` from attacker-controlled HEIF metadata. The saved allocation context at step 2 shows this block's `length` is 1, and the later EXIF-only branch shows `type` is treated as `"exif"`.

Libvips allocates a metadata buffer of exactly `length` bytes and fills it with the attacker-controlled metadata block. On the reproduced run this allocation is 1 byte long; ASan identifies this site as the origin of the region later overread.
Control step. Because the metadata block is treated as EXIF, libvips enters the branch that strips the 4-byte EXIF offset prefix. No `length >= 4` guard is checked before the next two state changes.

The EXIF trim path advances the metadata pointer by four bytes. Because step 2 allocated only 1 byte, this moves `data` to an address 3 bytes past the allocation's end before any further validation occurs.

Root cause. `length` is a `size_t`, so with the witnessed `length == 1` this subtraction wraps to a huge value instead of rejecting the short EXIF block. The later parse therefore sees a large length paired with the already invalid pointer from step 4.

On the EXIF branch, libvips names the blob `VIPS_META_EXIF_NAME` and stores the advanced pointer from step 4 plus the wrapped size from step 5 as image metadata. `vips_value_set_blob()` keeps that pointer/length pair by reference; it does not copy or repair the buffer.

fine_trace.code:
if( strcmp( name, VIPS_META_EXIF_NAME ) == 0 ) 
	if( vips__exif_parse( image ) )
fine_trace.note: Setting this metadata key automatically dispatches EXIF parsing. If the metadata had not been named `VIPS_META_EXIF_NAME` in step 6, the vulnerable libexif path would not run from `vips_image_set()`.

`vips__exif_parse()` reloads the same blob pointer and wrapped `size_t size` stored in step 6, then passes that wrapped `size_t` into `vips_exif_load_data_without_fix()`, whose parameter type is signed `int`.

The wrapped size forwarded in step 8 now crosses the second width boundary: `vips_exif_load_data_without_fix()` passes signed `int length` into libexif's `unsigned int ds` parameter. Libexif therefore receives a large positive `ds`, not the real 1-byte extent from step 2.

This short-buffer return would have rejected any real EXIF blob smaller than the 6-byte `ExifHeader`, but the wrapped `ds` from step 9 is large, so the check is bypassed. No later guard rechecks the actual allocation extent or the advanced pointer from step 4 before the header comparison.

Sink. `memcmp()` reads 6 bytes starting at the pointer advanced in step 4. ASan reports this as a heap-buffer-overflow read at `0x602000016a34`, 3 bytes to the right of the 1-byte allocation created in step 2.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_26524 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged 16389-byte HEIF witness to `smartcrop_fuzzer` and produced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 6 in exif_data_load_data`.

format.name: HEIF / HEIC image
format.contract: Exactly the staged 16389-byte HEIF file stored as `poc`. On the reproduced run, libheif exposed a metadata block typed `exif` whose reported size was 1 byte. `vips_foreign_load_heif_set_header()` nevertheless executed `data += 4; length -= 4`, so the auto-EXIF parser later received an out-of-bounds pointer together with a wrapped length and crashed in libexif's 6-byte EXIF-header `memcmp`.
